entities.summary:
Autocles (b. 500 BCE, Classical Athens) was a public servant or civil administrator of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Classical Athens. Known in the fields of military leaders & commanders.

Autocles played a crucial role in the Athenian administrative system, overseeing the city's military campaigns and strategic alliances. He was instrumental in the Athenian victory over the Persians at the Battle of Salamis in 480 BCE.

Autocles' legacy extends beyond his military achievements, as he contributed to the development of Athenian civic administration, establishing new standards for governance and public service.

The inscription on his tombstone, now lost to time, would have likely recorded his military victories and public service, providing a testament to his enduring impact on Athenian history.

As a testament to his significance, Autocles' name has been etched into the annals of history, symbolizing the importance of effective governance and military leadership in the Classical era.

In the words of the ancient Greek historian, 'Autocles, the Athenian statesman, whose military prowess and administrative acumen left an indelible mark on the city-state's trajectory.'
